fragments.text: I saw: Wrong type argument: stringp, :targets

reply_text:
㊥ (the stringp error) That error came from me, not from your config. It was a check I ran in your Emacs through emacsclient, and its error showed in your minibuffer. Nothing broke: the requires and the hot-reload refresh had already run before the error.

🈖 (cause) The check counted hot-reload targets by matching each element of `my-chatgpt-shell--hot-reload-resolve-files`'s result against a filename pattern. That function returns a property list, so one of the elements was the keyword `:targets`, and `string-match-p` refused it with `Wrong type argument: stringp, :targets`. My next check read the `:targets` list properly and found `turn-stepper.el`, `xiang-trace.el` and `xiaoxiang-preview.el` all in it.

㊟ (going forward) Errors from checks I run in your Emacs land in your minibuffer as if your config had failed. From here on I'll wrap such checks in `ignore-errors`, so a mistake in a check stays out of your way.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (a likely false alarm) When you switch the recorder back to `jvm`, `xiang-trace` may start reporting a violation. One of its rules is "reply end → dispatch", and it learns about dispatches by watching the Emacs function `session-mode--dispatch-analysis`. Under `jvm`, the JVM dispatches at send and Emacs never calls that function. So the lighter could show something like `!reply end → dispatch` while everything is fine. The fix is to have the JVM path record its own dispatch event: a small change in `session-turn-analysis.el`, which I can make if you see the warning.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (still open) The recorder is still `files` after the restart, so the fast path isn't in use. `(setq session-mode-turn-recorder 'jvm)` turns it back on. Once you've used it for a few turns, I'll measure the timing.
